title: TwoFactorSetup
wrapsNative: VStack with MonarchStepper over three steps: MonarchButton that opens the otpauth URL with openURL, MonarchCopyField for the setup key and a QR code from Core Image's the CIQRCodeGenerator CIFilter as an Image; MonarchOtpPinInput (the .oneTimeCode content type); MonarchRecoveryCodes
summary: A recipe, not a component: turn on two-step verification in three steps: connect an authenticator app, enter a code from it, and save the recovery codes.
whenToUse: In account security settings, when a person turns on two-step verification with an authenticator app.
whenNotToUse: To ask for a code at sign-in, use MonarchOtpPinInput alone. To re-confirm a signed-in person, use MonarchStepUpAuthDialog. For passkeys, use MonarchPasskeyManager.
api: MonarchButton("Open in authenticator app", systemImage: "key", variant: .primary, fullWidth: true) { openURL(otpauthURL) }
MonarchCopyField("Setup key", value: secret, isLabelHidden: true)
MonarchOtpPinInput("6-digit code", text: $code, error: codeError) { _ in verifyCode() }

states.name: connect
states.description: Open in authenticator app first, the setup key with a copy button, then the QR code for another device, and Next.

states.name: verify
states.description: A six-cell code field that fills from the keyboard's one-time code suggestion; an incomplete or rejected code shows the field's error.

states.name: recovery
states.description: The recovery codes with copy, save to file and the "I have saved my recovery codes" acknowledgement, which finishes the setup.

appearance: Existing Monarch components in the theme: the stepper's markers, a primary button, the copy field's monospaced key, the code cells and the recovery codes grid. The QR code stays black on white in every theme so scanners can read it.
platformNotes: The web's TwoFactorSetup is a dialog component with its own steps and messages, and the QR code first. On a phone the QR code is secondary, since the camera cannot scan the screen it is on: the otpauth link opens the authenticator app on the same device, and the setup key can be copied. iOS has a first-party QR generator in Core Image (the CIQRCodeGenerator filter), so the recipe draws the code itself, or the app passes an Image from its server. Present the recipe in a sheet with presentationDetents([.large]) when it starts from a settings row. Android composes the same recipe and draws or receives the QR code, because Android has no first-party generator.
accessibility: Each step title has the header trait; the stepper reads each step's position and name, such as "Step 2 of 3, Enter a code".
The QR code is one image element named "QR code for your authenticator app"; the setup key beside it gives the same data as text.
The setup key is a copy field whose button announces the copy.
The code field is one element named "6-digit code" with the code as its value; errors are shown and read in words.
The recovery codes are a named group with their own acknowledgement toggle.
edgeCases: Group the setup key in fours for reading, but copy and encode it without spaces in the otpauth link.
If no authenticator app is installed, opening the otpauth link fails; the setup key still works.
A rejected code usually means the device clock is wrong; say so in the error.
